steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Classical period prioritised clarity, balance and elegance — homophonic texture dominates, with clear melody above chordal accompaniment.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sonata form became the primary structure for first movements: exposition (two contrasting themes in different keys), development, recapitulation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Classical orchestra standardised: strings formed the core, with woodwind (flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon), horns, trumpets and timpani added.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Alberti bass is a broken-chord accompaniment pattern (low-high-middle-high) typical of Classical keyboard music — it provides harmonic and rhythmic support.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how classical music 1750-1820 are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use classical music 1750-1820. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use classical music 1750-1820 in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A detailed description using precise musical vocabulary (e.g. specific terms from the AQA elements list), referencing a named piece with accurate observations about how the elements are used and their | A comparison of two pieces identifying similarities and differences in how classical music 1750-1820 are used, explaining the different effects created in each musical context, using comparative langu | A practical application showing understanding of how classical music 1750-1820 can be manipulated in composition or performance, with specific examples of choices made and their intended effect.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use PRECISE musical vocabulary — not vague descriptions like it sounds nice Reference SPECIFIC musical elements when analysing any piece For listening questions: identify elements FIRST, then explain their effect For study pieces: know the context, structure and key features in detail For performing: focus on accuracy, expression and interpretation For composing: show development of ideas, not just repetition
